mechanism: Levodopa can cause nausea and vomiting leading to reduced potassium intake; carbidopa inhibits decarboxylase but does not directly affect potassium metabolism, though gastrointestinal effects may impair potassium absorption or increase losses.
action: Monitor serum potassium levels periodically in patients on chronic carbidopa-levodopa therapy, particularly those with nausea/vomiting or gastrointestinal disturbances; ensure adequate dietary potassium intake or supplement if hypokalemia develops.
